task_retrieval_key: A 43-year-old man visited the outpatient endocrine clinic at Tabriz University of Medical Sciences, Tabriz, Iran, accompanied by his sister, for an assessment of skin lesions. The patient exhibited multiple lesions on his shoulders, back, the lateral and medial parts of the dorsal surface of his feet, the medial and lateral malleus of both feet, and the dorsal and palmar surfaces of both hands. His siblings have been monitored in the same clinic for similar skin conditions. These conditions were characterized by palmar, eruptive, tuberous, and trauma site xanthomas, along with elevated levels of both total cholesterol and triglycerides in the plasma. Both parents had normal serum lipid levels. There was no history of coronary artery or other atherosclerotic disorders in the patient or his siblings. The patient reported no other complaints and maintained an active lifestyle as a greengrocer.
